kind_note: Not a repair campaign. No gen_configs.py grid, no run_experiments.py, no ideal comparison, and no scoring columns -- the CSVs here are one row per run of soak.py with resource and profile-counter columns instead. Nothing in this directory is comparable with the repair campaigns above it, and merge_experiments.py does not read it.
method: Recorded at run time, not reconstructed. The same session staged the code, launched both arms, watched them, and pulled the results down; commits, host state and the run window were read off the hosts rather than inferred from mtimes. Every sha below was verified against the hosts' checkouts after the run finished.
question: Whether moving SPOT translation and simplification in process, with a deadline honoured by abandoning the call to a detached worker, changes any repair and how it behaves over hours of campaign-scale concurrency. The differential suite compares one in-process answer against one tool answer, and check_engine_parity.py sets its timeouts far above anything that can fire; neither reaches a timeout that actually fires, concurrency at scale, or resource behaviour over hours.

profile_commit.subject: feat(scripts): add a 24-hour soak harness for the in-process libspot paths

profile_commit_evidence: Both hosts' worktrees were at this commit for the whole run and still are (`git rev-parse --short HEAD` on 2026-08-04 after close). There is no separate profile commit to distinguish from it: soak.py writes its own configurations from constants it carries, so the commit that fixed the harness also fixed the arms, tiers, run shapes and corpus order.
binary_commit_note: Recorded, not inferred: `counter --version` was captured into each arm's manifest.json at startup and reads commit=81a46a9, dirty=0 on both hosts. The binaries were never rebuilt during the run and the branch moved on without them, so they are pinned to this commit rather than tracking the branch. The commit is not an ancestor of main and will not become one: this archive landed on its own while feat/profiling-harness stayed unmerged, so the annotated tag provenance/libspot-soak is what holds it. Never delete that tag.

run_window.note: UTC. Both arms ran their full 24 hours and exited through their own budget check rather than being killed; the last line of each soak.log is `soak finished`. av3's clock skew (~17 min fast historically) is not corrected for here and does not matter: the arms are compared by digest, never by timestamp.

control.note: No timeouts at all, so both in-process calls run inline on the calling thread. This is the reference every digest is compared against.

deadline.note: Cycles the three tiers per round, as (ltl2tgba_timeout_ms, simplify_timeout_ms). loose is the correctness arm and must equal control; tight is the resource probe.

code_under_test: The in-process libspot paths on feat/profiling-harness: src/runner/spot_inprocess.cpp (translation and simplification through libspot behind one process-wide timed_mutex), the run_with_deadline abandonment used by both, and the profile counters in src/profile.cpp that make a firing deadline visible. src/runner/simplify_batcher.cpp did not exist at 81a46a9; its code was still inside src/runner/ltlfilt.cpp and was split out unchanged afterwards (125f0bc), verified behaviour-preserving by check_engine_parity.py.

results.correctness: 506 of 508 comparable loose-vs-control pairs agree (all 490 short pairs; 16 of 18 long). The two that disagree are both `lift` at gen40/pop1000, seeds 20260819 and 20260824, and neither fired a libspot deadline -- translate-timed-out and simplify-timed-out are zero on both sides -- so abandonment did not drop an individual in either.
results.resources: Peak resident set per short run: control median 77 MB, p99 13.2 GB, max 54 GB; loose 66 MB / 6.6 GB / 27 GB; mid 66 MB / 1.6 GB / 12 GB; tight 65 MB / 1.2 GB / 3.4 GB. The worst single run of the campaign is a control `lift` long run at 56 GB that completed successfully. Translation that used to sit in a killable child now runs in counter's own address space, so a firing deadline is the only thing bounding this, and it bounds the p99 by roughly 8-11x.
results.drift: None. Over four 6-hour buckets the floor of the sample series is flat (control p10 100 -> 105 -> 109 -> 114 MB; deadline 75 -> 73 -> 73 -> 73 MB), peak threads are constant at 9 (control) and 18 (deadline), peak descriptors stay near 21, and two orphaned tool processes were seen in 2,656 runs. Abandoned workers do not accumulate over a day of firing deadlines.
results.reversion: At parallel = 8 the single libspot lock keeps 85.7% of translations and 78.9% of simplifications in process in the control arm; the rest find the lock busy inside the 8 ms budget and spawn the tool. That fallback is what stops a fired deadline from starving the pool, and the lock-busy counters are what make it visible.
results.throughput: Short runs: control finishes 84% within its 5-minute cap over 13.2 wall hours, of which 10.4 are spent on runs that hit the cap having produced nothing. mid finishes 100% in 2.5 hours and returns more repairs per run (4.25 vs 3.89). tight also finishes 100% but changes the answer on 59% of comparable runs against mid's 10%.
results.firing_tiers: mid differs from control on 51 of 520 comparable runs (29 with fewer repairs, 13 with more); tight on 305 of 520 (141 fewer, 99 more).

caveats: The resource sampler polled once a second, not four times a second. The 0.25 s interval (ab2fe16, 'fix(scripts): sample the soak four times a second') was committed but never reached the hosts: both worktrees stayed at 81a46a9, and their soak.py hashes to f5a725f5, the 1.0 s revision. Rows are still written every 5 s either way, so the series cadence is unaffected -- but every peak_rss_kb is a lower bound taken from second-resolution polling, and most so on the short runs, whose median wall time is about 7 seconds. The bound understates every arm, so the comparison between tiers holds; the absolute peaks do not.

The two lift mismatches were unresolved when this directory was first written; the repro key now settles them. Seed 20260824 is withdrawn as evidence -- its baseline does not reproduce against itself. Seed 20260819 stands, at 1 differing digest in 5 loose repeats against a 5/5 stable baseline. Read the repro key, not the two MISMATCH lines in the analysis output, which predate it.

The loose tier fired five times in 606 runs -- four simplifications and one translation each exceeded 60 seconds -- and four of the five changed the answer. The tier was chosen as 'far above the worst call measured' and is not, which is the argument against reading any large timeout as equivalent to none.

A run killed at the wall cap dies on SIGKILL, so it skips the atexit profile report and writes no repairs: it has no profile JSON at all and hashes to the empty-set digest e3b0c44298fc1c14. The runs that most need the profiler are the ones without it. analyse_soak.py skips any pair where either side was capped; a digest mismatch read without that check is not a finding.

av2 carried two stray strace processes at ~52% CPU each (running since ~2026-07-29, unrelated to this work) plus two btop instances, so its wall times are noisy. No cross-host wall-clock comparison here is load-bearing, and none is drawn -- the arms are compared by digest and by per-run resource figures only.

Both hosts run ~/bin/ltl2tgba-reaper.sh on a 2-hourly cron, killing orphaned tools older than an hour, so the orphan census is bounded above by roughly two hours of accumulation rather than the whole run.

max_scoring_failure_rate is 0.95 in both arms. A firing translate deadline drops the individual, and the default 0.05 aborts a tight-tier run seconds in. It is set for both arms rather than the tight tier alone so the arms differ in the timeout keys and nothing else -- but it also means neither arm would have caught a scoring-failure regression.

layout.control/: runs.csv, samples.csv, manifest.json, context.txt (host state at launch: co-tenant processes, reaper cron, binary version), soak.log
layout.repro-lift-20260819/: reproduce_run.py output from av2: 5 repeats of lift gen40/pop1000 at seed 20260819, alternating the none and loose tiers
layout.repro-lift-20260824/: the same on av3 at seed 20260824

repro.why: The soak advances the seed every round, so it never repeats a configuration on one host and cannot separate 'the in-process path answers differently' from 'this run does not reproduce against itself'. These phases repeat one configuration 5 times per tier on the host that saw the mismatch.
repro.driver: scripts/reproduce_run.py, blob 850d4762b37908a41a0b5e9f41f7710daf19b3a6, verified still hashing to that on both hosts after the runs

binary_commit.evidence: counter --version in each phase's manifest.json, dirty=0; both hosts' counter-soak worktrees are checked out at this commit

repro.verdict: The two mismatches have different causes and only one is a finding.

repro-lift-20260819 (av2).reading: Baseline reproduces: none is 5/5 identical, 26 repairs and about 620 s every time. loose is 4/5, the one outlier being the second run executed. A genuine residual signal, but n=5, the repair count is unchanged, and the divergence is a re-ordering rather than a quality change.

repro-lift-20260824 (av3).reading: Not a mismatch. The none tier -- deadlines 0/0, so the mechanism under test is off -- produced 5 distinct digests in 5 repeats, with repairs 5/8/19/20/23 and wall 1056-2132 s. The configuration does not reproduce against itself, so the soak's disagreement for this seed is not evidence about deadlines or the in-process path. Most likely the solver timeouts (ltlsynt 10000 ms, black 1000 ms) making candidate drops wall-clock dependent on a long, high-variance run.

repro.limit: Neither tier is an out-of-process control: none and loose are both in-process libspot, differing only in deadline. These phases rule the DEADLINE MECHANISM in or out. They cannot separate 'in-process libspot perturbs results' from 'this run is timeout-sensitive'. A subprocess-engine arm is what would close that.
